subject: Commercial: advance credit, entity split, and tax evidence for Order Form
messages:
From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@astercloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form — payment cadence and tax evidence

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is ready to move forward pending final commercial language. A few items procurement & legal asked us to confirm before we can sign:

- AsterCloud will need the option to prepay a portion of the annual commit (advance credit) and have invoices reflect the consumed portion monthly. Can Redwood issue an invoice on receipt of payment and then provide consumption-based credits?
- Tax: our AP team needs a copy of Redwood's tax residency certificate (or instructions for VAT handling). We will also provide our own certificate.
- Entity routing: We will be splitting payments across two AsterCloud entities. Need clarity on invoice entity and whether Redwood can split invoices accordingly.

We're attaching our standard PO template and the tax certificate. Can you share a redline of the Order Form addressing advance credit and split invoicing?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Nguyen
Director, Procurement
AsterCloud

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@astercloud.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — payment cadence and tax evidence

Lisa —

Appreciate the quick list. We can accommodate advance prepayment + monthly consumption credits; I'll outline the mechanics and loop Legal for the exact clause language. High-level proposal:

- Customer may prepay up to 100% of the committed spend as an "Advance Credit." Redwood will issue an invoice upon receipt of payment (Taxed according to billing entity rules).
- Monthly consumption will be reconciled against Advance Credit; Redwood will provide a monthly statement showing tokens consumed and remaining credit.
- If the Advance Credit is exhausted, consumption will be billed on Net 30 terms thereafter unless otherwise agreed.
- For entity split: Redwood can issue split invoices if entity details and tax IDs are provided in advance; however, advance payment must make clear which entity(ies) hold the credit balance.

I'm attaching an annotated Order Form (OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf) showing where we'd insert the advance-credit mechanics and invoice-split options. Could you confirm which entity will remit the initial advance?

I'll ask Legal (cc'd Jordan) to propose language for the invoicing and tax-residency confirmation. Grace, can you pull the tax certificate template and confirm Redwood's tax evidence we should provide?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@astercloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T14:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — payment cadence and tax evidence

Markus / Lisa —

Thanks for the context. From Legal's side, a few clarifications and proposed redline notes:

1) Advance Credit mechanics:
   - We should add an "Advance Credit Account" section in the Order Form that defines (i) how funds are applied; (ii) reconciliation cadence; and (iii) expiration (suggest 12 months from receipt unless otherwise agreed).
   - Require that Redwood's invoice for receipt of advance explicitly notes the tax treatment (VAT/GST applied where required).

2) Invoice splitting & entity routing:
   - We can support split invoicing provided AsterCloud supplies full billing entity names, addresses, and tax IDs.
   - To avoid allocation disputes, include a required "Allocation Schedule" appendix where the parties list percentage splits or fixed amounts per entity.

3) Net terms fallback:
   - We prefer to keep Net 30 as the default for non-prepaid consumption. If the advance is consumed and invoices remain unpaid, standard late interest and invoice remedies apply (we'll keep this standard).

4) Tax evidence:
   - Redwood can share a US tax residency letter (pdf). We'll request AsterCloud's tax certificate and confirm whether reverse charge applies.

Action items: Markus to provide the redline (done); Grace to attach Redwood tax letter and an example allocation schedule; Lisa to confirm which entity will remit and to share billing details.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks — attached is the filled allocation worksheet and our confirmation that Entity A (AsterCloud, Inc.) will remit the initial advance (80%) and Entity B (AsterCloud EMEA Ltd) will remit 20% and expects split invoicing.

We reviewed your redline and have two quick asks before we sign:

1) Could Redwood shorten the Advance Credit expiry from 12 months to 9 months? Our finance policy requires shorter consumption windows for prepaid credits.
2) On invoice heads: EMEA requires VAT reverse charge treatment; we'll attach guidance from our tax counsel in a follow-up.

We are close — if Legal can accept the 9-month expiry and confirm the split-invoicing mechanics, procurement will issue the PO and we can complete DocuSign.

DocuSign link to be expected after legal alignment.

Best,
Lisa

AsterCloud
